payload.purpose_context: Consumers building in languages Spec Kitty has no specialist guidance for (Zig, Go, ...) currently get a mission review that always fails its Python-only dead-code gate and a charter context that labels them Python. This mission makes the unknown-language path honest and neutral: the gate reports itself not applicable, unknown languages resolve to an explicit unknown value with tech-agnostic guidance and an advisory to extend the local charter, and a corrected interview answer takes effect on regeneration.
payload.purpose_tldr: Non-Python projects get an honest, language-neutral review and charter context instead of false Python failures and labels.

payload.question: How should an unknown/unrecognised project language be represented?

payload.final_answer: Reserved unknown token: catalog.languages [unknown] when a declared language is unrecognised; admits no language-scoped artifacts; context renders Languages: unknown plus a one-line charter-extension advisory; no-language-declared keeps None (admit-all).

payload.question: How should a corrected interview answer take effect on an existing charter (#4614)?

payload.final_answer: --from-interview re-derives: only charter generate --from-interview derives languages from the fresh interview; runtime readers keep compiled-first precedence; activate/pack recompiles preserve the recorded value.

payload.question: Dead-code gate on a change set with no supported files: outcome shape?

payload.final_answer: Skip gate + NA note: gate recorded skip; non-failing dead_code_not_applicable finding (MISSION_REVIEW_DEAD_CODE_NOT_APPLICABLE) naming unsupported extensions + charter-extension remediation; verdict pass_with_notes.
#4613 hyphenated compounds (minimal) and the review pytest pre-check; available_tools registry NOT widened (validation stays strict, only de-conflated from language detection).

payload.question: Doctrine is scoped to languages the detector does not know (go/csharp): how to handle?

payload.final_answer: Doctrine-derived vocabulary: a language named (whole-word, casefolded) in the languages/frameworks answer counts as recognised when any active doctrine artifact is scoped to it; no hardcoded per-language additions; unknown means no specialist guidance exists.

payload.wp_title: Compile wiring - from-interview re-derives languages; tool diagnostics
Language authority - unknown detection, doctrine vocabulary, hyphen rule, precedence parameter
Review - dead-code gate not applicable + pytest pre-check warning
Reserved unknown vocabulary, validator guard, catalog-miss advice, advisory text

payload.question: How to remediate wrongly-scoped language-independent tactics?

payload.final_answer: New WP, all 3 tactics: remove applies_to_languages from secure-regex, chain-of-responsibility and dependency-hygiene (label language examples, strip in-house repo paths/Sonar ids), close the bias-test scope loophole, drop the stale neutrality allowlist entry, regenerate-graph; accept a rebase against PR #5324.

payload.question: With scopes removed, keep the doctrine-derived vocabulary?

payload.final_answer: Keep it: the provider recognises languages genuinely language-specific artifacts are scoped to (python, java, javascript, typescript, php, twig, html, css after de-scoping); tests use synthetic overlays, not shipped pack scopes.

payload.wp_title: De-scope language-independent built-in tactics; close the bias-gate scope loophole

payload.question: Which interview answers decide the project language?

payload.final_answer: Declared answer wins: when the languages/frameworks answer is a real declaration, resolve from it alone (built-in words + doctrine vocabulary combined); nothing matched -> [unknown]; other answers only scanned when that answer is empty/default/placeholder.

payload.question: Show the advisory for recognised languages without scoped doctrine (rust/swift/ruby)?

payload.final_answer: Advisory whenever the resolved languages have no installed doctrine scoped to them (unknown or e.g. [rust]); stored catalog.languages unchanged.
